Title: Settings user creation produces orgless accounts
Description: Settings-created users are saved without organization_id while authenticated orgless users are rejected.
Business Impact: New staff accounts can be unusable after creation.
Security Impact: Improper provisioning can bypass intended organization lifecycle controls.
Data Integrity Impact: Users can exist without required tenant context.
Financial Impact: Operational staff cannot access paid/finance workflows after creation.
Reproduction Steps: Create a user through settings, then authenticate and request any protected route.
Expected Result: User receives organization and reaches permitted dashboard.
Actual Result: User lacks organization_id and middleware aborts 403.
Evidence: SettingsController omits organization_id; Fortify CreateNewUser contains separate org-aware logic.
Recommended Correction: Use one org-aware provisioning service/action and require or inherit organization.
Required Tests: Creation-to-login tests for every role, orgless rejection, active/inactive state.
Root Cause: Two independent creation paths disagreed on the two fields that determine whether an account works. SettingsController never set organization_id and defaulted active_status to false; Fortify CreateNewUser inherited the org and defaulted to true.
Correction Summary: UserProvisioningService is now the single creation path for both. Resolves organisation without guessing, refuses cross-tenant provisioning by non-superusers, validates target org exists and is active, normalises email, guards duplicates, assigns role transactionally, sets active status and email verification deliberately, and asserts as a post-condition that the returned account has both organisation and role.
Validation Result: 12/12 pass including creation-to-authenticated-request end to end and the settings HTTP path; full suite 1194 passed / 13 skipped.
Residual Risk: Invitation and import paths were not found in this codebase; if added later they must route through the same service. No CI guard yet prevents a third creation path appearing.

Title: Core farm writes are not deny-by-default
Method or Route: health, medications, mating, farrowing, weaning, pigs, weights, feed-production, structures, rooms
Description: Many operational write routes sit behind only broad auth/session/activity middleware and sampled controllers lack authorization calls.
Business Impact: Low-privilege users can alter livestock, medical, inventory or facility records by direct URL.
Security Impact: Broken access control on critical operations.
Data Integrity Impact: Unauthorized changes can corrupt livestock and inventory records.
Financial Impact: Downstream cost, stock and sale records can become unreliable.
Reproduction Steps: Log in as a non-operational role and POST to an unguarded route such as health/store-health or feed-production/mix.
Expected Result: Request is denied unless role/permission explicitly allows it.
Actual Result: Route has no role/permission middleware and controller has no internal policy check.
Evidence: Grep for authorize/hasPermission/abort_unless in sampled controllers returned no enforcement.
Recommended Correction: Create route/action permission matrix and apply middleware or policies at every boundary.
Required Tests: Direct request role matrix tests for all create/update/delete/export routes.
Root Cause: No farm-operations permission catalogue existed (finance 51 / sales 2 / storefront 15 only), so 65 routes across 7 controllers with zero internal authorization had nothing to gate them with.
Correction Summary: Created FarmOperationsPermissionsSeeder (16 permissions across livestock/facilities/feed) and gated all 65 routes, splitting read from destructive write. Also fixed 6 broken facade delegations and a NavigationHelper 500 found during the work.
Validation Result: State-changing non-finance routes without route middleware 89 -> 59; all 59 remaining verified as policy-enforced, superuser-guarded or customer-owned. Full suite 1234 passed / 13 skipped.
Residual Risk: Gates are route-level; per-record ownership for health/feed/facilities is not yet policy-checked (Phase 6). No CI guard yet asserts new routes carry a gate.

Title: Finance confidentiality is incomplete
Description: The finance comment promises an outer role layer, but the route group has no outer finance middleware and several finance routes lack view_finance.
Business Impact: Users may see sensitive finance records by URL.
Security Impact: Confidential balances, suppliers and payment data can be exposed.
Data Integrity Impact: Unauthorized reads can drive operational mistakes.
Financial Impact: Financial statements, payments and reconciliations can be disclosed.
Reproduction Steps: Log in as same-organization user without finance permission and request unwrapped finance URLs.
Expected Result: Finance data requires view_finance or narrower permission.
Actual Result: Several routes are unwrapped by permission middleware.
Evidence: Static route inspection shows mixed protection with no outer finance gate.
Recommended Correction: Apply finance-wide view gate plus narrower action permissions.
Required Tests: Role matrix tests for every finance route and export/download/AJAX path.
Root Cause: Route::prefix('finance') had no outer middleware despite a comment promising one, and 69 of 207 finance routes carried no permission gate at all.
Correction Summary: Added EnsureFinanceAccess outer boundary (any admitted-module permission, NOT view_finance -- farmmanager/mill_operator hold narrow finance permissions without it) plus per-route gates on all 69 previously ungated routes. Read gates follow each seeder's documented intent rather than a blanket view_finance.
Validation Commands: php artisan route:list --except-vendor --json (middleware coverage measurement); php artisan test
Validation Result: Ungated finance routes 69 -> 0; all 207 behind outer boundary; 472 routes unchanged; 21 new tests pass; full suite 1194 passed / 13 skipped.
Regression Result: No regressions after correcting two self-inflicted issues (route ordering, static memo) and two over-restrictive gates.
Residual Risk: Gate correctness depends on the seeded permission catalogue. A new finance route added without a gate is still admitted by the outer boundary to any finance-permission holder, so route-gate coverage should be asserted in CI (Phase 8).

Title: Finance attachment downloads lack finance permission
Description: Attachment downloads check organization and file existence but not view_finance or parent view permission.
Business Impact: Financial evidence files can be downloaded by same-organization users without finance access.
Security Impact: Sensitive documents can leak.
Data Integrity Impact: Attachment access can bypass parent-record security.
Financial Impact: Payment, receipt, invoice or refund evidence can be disclosed.
Reproduction Steps: Request /finance/attachments/{id}/download as same-org non-finance user.
Expected Result: Download denied unless finance view permission passes.
Actual Result: Download path has no finance permission check.
Evidence: Controller comment states download requires view_finance but method does not enforce it.
Recommended Correction: Require view_finance or parent-specific view policy for download.
Required Tests: Cross-role, cross-org and ID enumeration tests.
Root Cause: download() checked organisation and file existence only, never view_finance or any parent permission, despite the class docblock claiming otherwise.
Correction Summary: Parent-aware authorizeReadFor() requiring the parent's view OR write permission, driven by a single PARENT_MAP. Also fixed two fail-OPEN paths in ensureInOrg() (unresolvable org returned early; null parent organization_id passed) -- both now deny.
Validation Result: Download now denies without parent entitlement; org guard fails closed in both previously-open branches.
Residual Risk: Dedicated per-parent-type download tests still to be added in Phase 7; current evidence is the org/permission logic plus full-suite regression.

Title: Organisation isolation is transitional and permissive
Description: Operational models avoid global scope, policies pass null organization resources, and bindings use global findOrFail.
Business Impact: A user may access another organization record through unguarded direct URLs.
Security Impact: Cross-tenant data exposure risk.
Data Integrity Impact: Tenant data may be modified across boundaries.
Financial Impact: Cross-tenant finance/inventory reports may be wrong.
Reproduction Steps: Use Organization A user with Organization B pig/farrowing/mating/weaning ID on unguarded routes.
Expected Result: All access fails closed.
Actual Result: Some bindings and policy fallbacks do not scope or fail closed.
Evidence: Static inspection confirms global binding and null-pass policy behavior.
Recommended Correction: Backfill and require organization_id, scope bindings, fail closed on null, add global/local scopes consistently.
Required Tests: Cross-organization list/view/update/delete/download/export tests.
Root Cause: EnforcesOrganizationScope::sameOrganization() returned TRUE for any resource whose organization_id was null or absent. Framed in the register as transitional, but 41 of 128 tables carry no organization_id column at all -- including farrowing, matings, weanings, health_records, pig_weights -- so for those the exemption was permanent and FarrowingPolicy/MatingPolicy/WeaningPolicy enforced no tenant boundary whatsoever.
Correction Summary: Made the scope guard fail closed. Added a ResolvesOrganization contract so column-less models derive tenancy through their parent pig, implemented on Farrowing (sow then boar), Mating (female then male) and Weaning (pig then mother). Added a creating hook to BelongsToOrganization that stamps the current organisation, and applied the trait to PigManagement, PigSale, PigDeath and PurchaseRequest so no write path produces unscoped rows. Added a corrective backfill migration.
Tests Updated: OrganizationScopePolicyTest (inverted the assertion that locked in the fail-open contract); PigSalePolicyTest and PurchaseRequestPolicyTest (organisation added to in-memory stand-ins)
Validation Commands: php artisan migrate/migrate:rollback on MariaDB 11.4.2 with seeded null rows; php artisan test
Validation Result: Cross-tenant access to farrowing/mating/weaning now denied (was allowed). Backfill verified on MariaDB: 3 unscoped rows -> 0, re-run wrote nothing (idempotent), rollback is a documented no-op. Full suite 1234 passed / 13 skipped.
Regression Result: 11 failures surfaced and all resolved at cause rather than by weakening assertions: 3 models gained the trait, and in-memory policy stand-ins were given an organisation.
Residual Risk: organization_id remains NULLABLE on all 87 tables that have it; NOT NULL constraints are deliberately NOT added yet as that needs production validation that zero nulls remain. 41 tables still have no column and rely on derived resolution. health_records, pig_weights, medication_administrations and piglet_deaths have no policy at all yet, so derived resolution is available but unused for them (Phase 6). Route model bindings for pig/farrowing/mating/weaning remain unscoped -- policies now deny, but binding still resolves cross-tenant records before the policy runs.

Title: Order confirmation can oversell or double-reserve
Description: Confirmation does not lock order/listing rows, silently accepts already-reserved pig listings and clamps negative product stock to zero.
Business Impact: Two customers can be confirmed for one pig or final product units.
Security Impact: Concurrency flaw in commerce state transition.
Data Integrity Impact: Stock availability can be corrupted.
Financial Impact: Revenue/orders may exceed real stock.
Reproduction Steps: Create competing pending orders for same listing and confirm concurrently on separate DB connections.
Expected Result: One confirmation succeeds and the other rejects conflict.
Actual Result: Code has no lock/reload/conflict rejection path.
Evidence: Static source lacks lockForUpdate and negative stock rejection.
Recommended Correction: Lock order and listings, revalidate under lock, make transition idempotent and reject conflicts.
Required Tests: True multi-connection concurrency tests for pig and product stock.

Actual Result: No provider refund API method or refund reconciliation exists.
Evidence: Source inspection confirms missing refund API surface.

Required Tests: Paystack sandbox refund success, pending, failure and duplicate tests.

Title: COD completion can mark orders paid with skipped finance lines
Description: COD completion skips unlinked order lines then unconditionally sets payment_status to paid.
Business Impact: Orders can appear paid/completed before finance settlement exists.

Expected Result: Completion should block or enter settlement-pending state.
Actual Result: Code records a note and still marks payment paid.
Evidence: Static source shows skipped unlinked lines are not fatal.

Title: Key schedules are not registered
Description: Active schedule list contains only finance events and storefront sync, while Kernel-only schedules are absent.
Business Impact: Reminders, notifications, invoice reconciliation and loan interest may not run.
Security Impact: Operational controls relying on schedules fail silently.
Data Integrity Impact: Time-sensitive livestock/finance state can stale.
Financial Impact: Interest and reconciliation postings can be missed.
Reproduction Steps: Run env CACHE_STORE=array php artisan schedule:list and compare App\\Console\\Kernel.
Expected Result: All intended schedules appear in active schedule list.
Actual Result: Only two active schedules are listed.
Evidence: Command output plus Kernel source confirms orphaned schedules.
Recommended Correction: Move schedules to active Laravel 11 bootstrap path or bind kernel.
Required Tests: schedule:list regression and command invocation tests.
Root Cause: App\Console\Kernel::schedule() held five schedules, but Laravel's slimmed bootstrap never loads that class -- bootstrap/app.php points commands: at routes/console.php, so the framework's own ConsoleKernel is used and the application Kernel was dead code.
Correction Summary: Migrated all five schedules to routes/console.php with withoutOverlapping, onOneServer, explicit timezone, descriptions and onFailure logging. Deleted the dead Kernel class so the trap cannot be reset. Guarded emailOutputOnFailure, which the original called with a config key that is unset by default.
Validation Commands: php artisan schedule:list; php artisan test
Validation Result: schedule:list now shows 7 tasks (was 2): weights:notify, gestation:notify, notifications:process, finance:reconcile-invoice-aggregates, finance:accrue-loan-interest plus the two pre-existing provider-registered tasks.
Residual Risk: onOneServer requires a lock-capable cache store; the production database store supports locks but a switch to a non-locking store would silently disable it. No alerting is wired beyond log records and the optional failure email.

Title: Laravel 11 is outside security support
Description: composer.lock pins Laravel v11.45.1; official Laravel policy ended 11.x security fixes on 12 March 2026.
Business Impact: Production launch begins on unsupported framework.
Security Impact: Security patches are no longer provided for framework branch.
Data Integrity Impact: Framework bugs may remain unpatched.
Financial Impact: Incident/remediation costs increase.
Reproduction Steps: Check composer.lock and Laravel official support policy on 28 July 2026.
Expected Result: Framework version is under active security support.
Actual Result: Laravel 11 security support ended before assessment date.
Evidence: Official Laravel release policy and lockfile.
Recommended Correction: Upgrade to supported Laravel version and retest.
Required Tests: Full regression suite, dependency audit and deployment rehearsal after upgrade.
Root Cause: composer.json pinned laravel/framework ^11.31. Laravel 11 security support ended 12 March 2026 per the official support policy; the assessment date is 28 July 2026.
Correction Summary: Upgraded Laravel 11.45.1 -> 13.23.0 (two majors). Target chosen from the official policy fetched at implementation time: Laravel 12 leaves bug-fix support on 13 Aug 2026 (16 days out) so it is not a defensible target for a new launch; Laravel 13 has bug fixes to Q3 2027 and security to 17 Mar 2028. Also raised php constraint ^8.2 -> ^8.3 (L13 minimum), jetstream ^5.3 -> ^5.5, tinker ^2.9 -> ^3.0, phpunit ^11.0 -> ^13.0. Composer held livewire on 3.x (3.6.4 -> 3.8.2, minor), so the Blade/Livewire template layer was untouched. No --ignore-platform-reqs used.
Tests Updated: tests/Feature/Policies/PigSalePolicyTest.php (5 x @dataProvider annotation -> #[DataProvider] attribute; PHPUnit 13 removed doc-comment annotation support)
Validation Commands: composer validate --no-check-publish; php artisan about; php artisan route:list --except-vendor; php artisan event:list; php artisan config:cache; php artisan route:cache; php artisan view:cache; php artisan event:cache; php artisan optimize:clear; php artisan test; php artisan migrate:fresh (MariaDB 11.4.2); composer audit; php -l x942
Validation Result: Laravel 13.23.0 boots on PHP 8.4.22. 472 routes (unchanged). Suite: 1161 passed / 13 skipped / 3442 assertions - EXACT baseline parity. 188/188 migrations pass on MariaDB. composer audit: 0 advisories (was 36). All caches build and clear. 942 PHP files lint clean.
Regression Result: No regressions. Test count, skip count and assertion count all identical to the pre-upgrade baseline.
Residual Risk: Livewire remains on 3.x; a future Livewire 4 migration is a separate scoped effort. Laravel 13 upgrade guide review for deprecated APIs beyond those surfaced by the suite should be revisited if runtime deprecations appear in production logs.

Title: First-use document sequence allocation can race
Description: Missing sequence row is created without unique-conflict retry; test is sequential despite name.
Business Impact: First simultaneous writers can fail or allocate unreliably.
Security Impact: Race can cause failed user workflows.
Data Integrity Impact: Document sequence creation can collide.
Financial Impact: Invoices/receipts/orders can fail under first live use.
Reproduction Steps: Start two first writers for same org/type/year on separate DB connections.
Expected Result: One creates row; the other retries and allocates next number.
Actual Result: Code relies on create then lock, no retry.
Evidence: Unique key exists but application lacks conflict handling.
Recommended Correction: Use atomic insert/upsert with conflict retry then lock/increment.
Required Tests: True multi-connection first-use tests.
Root Cause: next() locked an existing sequence row FOR UPDATE but created a missing row with an unguarded create(). Two first writers for the same (org, type, year) both insert and the unique key rejects one.
Correction Summary: Replaced create() with insertOrIgnore followed by a re-select under lock, so the loser of the race adopts the winner's row. lockSequence() now orders by id, which also contains a second defect: MySQL treats NULLs as DISTINCT in a unique index, so global (org-less) sequences have no duplicate protection at all -- ordering makes every allocator converge on one row regardless.
Validation Commands: vendor/bin/phpunit -c phpunit.concurrency.xml (8 concurrent OS processes against MariaDB 11.4.2)
Validation Result: Fixed: 8 workers, 8 unique contiguous numbers, 0 failures. Defect reintroduced: 2 of 3 tests fail with UniqueConstraintViolationException 1062 Duplicate entry. Verified in BOTH directions.
Residual Risk: ISOLATION-DEPENDENT, and the register does not record this. Under InnoDB's default REPEATABLE READ, a FOR UPDATE matching no rows takes a gap lock that serialises the insert, so the original defect was NOT reproducible there. It reproduces under READ COMMITTED, which is common in production and which the app does not pin in config/database.php. Pinning the isolation level explicitly would remove the dependence on server configuration.

Title: Storefront order and customer references use count plus one
Description: Identifiers derive from current row counts.
Business Impact: Concurrent creation can collide and deleted rows can create confusing references.
Security Impact: Reference collision can expose errors to users.
Data Integrity Impact: Unique constraints may reject otherwise valid transactions.
Financial Impact: Order/customer creation can fail under load.
Reproduction Steps: Create two orders or customers concurrently in same organization.
Expected Result: Each receives unique reference without failure.
Actual Result: Both can calculate same next reference before insert.
Evidence: Source uses count()+1.
Recommended Correction: Use shared atomic sequence service or DB sequence with retry.
Required Tests: Concurrent checkout/customer creation tests.
Root Cause: Business identifiers derived from row counts. Concurrent writers read the same count and derive the same value against uniquely-keyed columns; deletions shift the series permanently.
Correction Summary: Created StorefrontReferenceAllocator delegating to NumberingService, and routed every count-based generator through it. The register names 2 sites; a repository sweep found 5. Critically, CheckoutService and QuoteService BOTH minted 'SO-' order references from independent counts on the same uniquely-keyed table, so a checkout and a quote conversion could mint the same reference -- they now share one sequence. Also fixed PigStockService's MAX(id)+1 pig code, whose own docblock had deferred the race pending a counter table that now exists. Each allocation passes initialNumber seeded from existing data so live series continue instead of restarting at 1 and colliding.
Validation Commands: grep sweep for count()+1 and max()+1; php artisan test
Validation Result: Zero count-based identifier generators remain in app/. Full suite 1243 passed / 13 skipped.
Residual Risk: These sequences use year 0 to denote a continuous non-annual series, because the reference formats carry no year. If a future requirement wants annual reset, the sequence key must change and existing references migrated. No dedicated concurrency test yet covers the storefront reference allocator specifically -- it shares the NumberingService path that is covered.

Title: Finance outbox lacks atomic claiming and retries
Description: Job selects pending events without row lock or processing claim and uses tries=1.
Business Impact: Multiple workers can duplicate work or strand failed events.
Security Impact: Operational monitoring cannot rely on job status.
Data Integrity Impact: Event status can become terminal without recovery.
Financial Impact: Finance postings may be delayed or need manual repair.
Reproduction Steps: Run two workers over same pending event batch or force subscriber failure.
Expected Result: Events are atomically claimed, retried and recoverable.
Actual Result: No claim/lease/retry/dead-letter path in job.
Evidence: Static code selects pending get() and logs failures.
Recommended Correction: Add claim leases, retries, backoff, dead-letter, replay and metrics.
Required Tests: Multi-worker duplicate, failure and replay tests.
Root Cause: Two separate issues under one finding. (a) No claim: pending events were selected with a plain get() and processed with no lease, so concurrent workers duplicated effort. (b) Failure was terminal: with tries=1 and no retry scheduling, ANY transient fault (lock-wait timeout, dropped connection, deadlock) moved an event to 'failed' permanently, silently dropping a finance posting with nothing surfacing it.
Correction Summary: Added OutboxClaimer with an atomic guarded-UPDATE claim, per-event retry with exponential backoff, a dead-letter ceiling, stale-claim recovery for dead workers, and backlog counters. Added 'processing' status plus claimed_at/claimed_by/next_retry_at/last_error_at columns. 'failed' now means dead-lettered and actionable rather than 'anything went wrong once'.
Validation Commands: vendor/bin/phpunit -c phpunit.concurrency.xml (6 processes vs MariaDB 11.4.2, run 3x); php artisan test
Validation Result: Exclusive claiming proven across 6 concurrent processes over 60 events: zero double-claims. In-flight claims not reclaimable. Stale claims recovered 3/3. Concurrency suite stable over 3 consecutive runs. Full suite 1243 passed / 13 skipped.
Regression Result: No regressions. Two defects of my own were caught by these tests: a per-instance claim token that made a second claim() re-return the first batch, and double-counted processing_attempts (claimer and Subscriber::markEvent both incremented).
Residual Risk: SELECT..FOR UPDATE in NumberingService deadlocked under sustained multi-process load (SQLSTATE 40001/1213); resolved with DB::transaction attempts:5. The same deadlock class may exist in other locking paths not yet load-tested. No operator-facing outbox dashboard or alert wiring yet -- backlog() exposes the counters but nothing consumes them (Phase 8). Duplicate-journal protection continues to rest on the journal_postings idempotency key, which was verified present.

Title: Finance attachment parent support is inconsistent
Description: Routes allow receipts/invoices/refunds but resolver also supports vendor-invoices/payments; Payment has no write permission mapping.
Business Impact: Supported behavior is unclear and some parents cannot be safely attached.
Security Impact: Authorization gaps may appear when routes expand.
Data Integrity Impact: Attachment records can become inconsistent with parent permissions.
Financial Impact: Payment evidence handling is incomplete.
Reproduction Steps: Compare route type regex with resolver and permission mapping.
Expected Result: Supported parent types and permission map align.
Actual Result: Resolver and routes/mapping disagree.
Evidence: Static source evidence.
Recommended Correction: Align route types, parent policies and permission mapping.
Required Tests: Upload/download/delete tests for every parent type.
Root Cause: Three sources disagreed: route regex allowed receipts|invoices|refunds, resolveParent() also accepted vendor-invoices and payments, and authorizeWriteFor() had no Payment mapping so Payment attachments were permanently unwritable.
Correction Summary: Single PARENT_MAP constant is now the sole source of truth; the route {type} constraint is derived from it via supportedTypePattern(), and both read and write permissions come from the same entry.
Validation Commands: php artisan route:list; php artisan test
Validation Result: Route constraint, resolver and permission map derive from one map and cannot drift; Payment is now a supported parent for both read and write.

Title: Locked NPM dependencies have advisories
Description: npm audit reports 13 vulnerabilities: 1 critical, 10 high, 2 moderate.
Business Impact: Vulnerable packages may affect build/dev tooling or runtime bundling.
Security Impact: Known dependency vulnerabilities remain unresolved.
Data Integrity Impact: No direct app data corruption shown.
Financial Impact: Incident/remediation risk remains.
Reproduction Steps: Run npm audit --audit-level=low.
Expected Result: No high/critical advisories in release lockfile.
Actual Result: Audit exits non-zero with 13 advisories.
Evidence: npm audit output lists shell-quote critical plus axios/vite/etc high advisories.
Recommended Correction: Upgrade lockfile and run audit in CI.
Required Tests: Dependency audit gate tests.
Root Cause: Lockfile pinned build-tooling packages predating published advisories; the final 4 advisories all chained from a single upstream defect (brace-expansion <=5.0.7 DoS) reached via tailwindcss 3.4.17 -> sucrase -> glob -> minimatch, which npm audit fix could not resolve without a Tailwind v4 major upgrade.
Correction Summary: Ran npm audit fix (no --force, per remediation constraints) resolving 9 of 13. Resolved the remaining 4 with a surgical package.json override pinning brace-expansion ^5.0.8, avoiding a Tailwind 3->4 major migration across 290 Blade views. Result: 13 advisories -> 0.
Validation Commands: npm audit fix; npm audit --audit-level=low; npm run build
Validation Result: npm audit: found 0 vulnerabilities (was 13: 1 critical/10 high/2 moderate). npm run build: SUCCESS, vite 6.4.3, 56 modules transformed, manifest.json with 2 entries.

Title: Non-functional try/catch around Blueprint index creation in legacy reporting index migration
Description: Each index addition wraps $table->index(...) in try/catch inside the Schema::table closure. The closure only queues Blueprint commands; SQL executes after the closure returns, so the try/catch cannot catch duplicate-key errors. The stated idempotency guard is inoperative.
Business Impact: A re-run on a schema that already has these indexes would fail the deployment rather than being skipped as designed.
Security Impact: None.
Data Integrity Impact: None directly; risks aborting a deploy mid-migration.
Financial Impact: None directly.
Reproduction Steps: Inspect the migration; note try/catch placement relative to Blueprint execution. Re-run migration against a schema already carrying the named indexes.
Expected Result: Existing indexes are detected and skipped without error.
Actual Result: Guard is inoperative; duplicate key error would surface at blueprint build time.
Evidence: Source inspection plus MariaDB verification that the migration executes and creates pigs_management_date_of_birth_idx.
Recommended Correction: Replace try/catch with a real index-existence check via the schema manager before adding.
Required Tests: Migration re-run test on MariaDB against a schema already carrying the indexes.
Root Cause: Misunderstanding of Laravel Blueprint deferred execution semantics.
